title: Starter Infer: velocity snippets & pricing tests
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures short, testable messaging and pricing experiments aimed at increasing developer activation for the Hosted API. Focus: convey the developer-first velocity (time-to-prototype), predictable economics for early usage, and safe upgrade path to Dedicated/Private when customers scale.

Audience:
- Engineering-first developers evaluating hosted inference for prototypes and early product usage
- Platform/infra leads who care about latency/cost tradeoffs

Primary goal:
- Lift 7‑day activation rate (API keys used for >1 meaningful call) by 12% and reduce first-hour dropoff by 20% through clearer quickstart and cost language.

High-level positioning hooks (short variants for banners, hero lines, emails):
- "Prototype LLM features in minutes — production inference when you need it."
- "Start with a predictable API, scale with control: pay-as-you-go or reserved capacity."
- "Low-lift integration, transparent token economics, and upgrade paths for scale."

Core developer value props (bulleted copy to test):
- Instant sandbox: get API keys and run a generation or embedding with a single curl in <3 minutes.
- Predictable unit economics: clear per-token pricing + estimator so devs know cost before running test suites.
- Performance out of the box: models and runtimes selected to balance latency and cost for common dev workloads.
- Safe growth: bump to Dedicated capacity without rewriting code when you move from prototype to production.

Quickstart angles to A/B test on landing and docs:
1) Fast proof: "3-minute curl -> sample app" (focus: immediate success, includes micro-example + estimated cost for 1 request).
2) Low-cost sandbox: "Try with free credits + cost estimator" (focus: reassure about runaway costs and show estimator screenshot).
3) Production-ready sample: "Ship with canary rollouts" (focus: how same API supports canaries and model pins).

Sample quickstart script (short copy for a hero card):
- "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{
    "model": "rw-medium-1",
    "prompt": "Summarize: <paste text>" 
  }'
  -> response in ~200ms; estimated cost: $0.0008 per request (example)."

Pricing-language drafts (aim: clarity over precision; testable variants):
Variant A — Transparent meter: "Pay per token. Billing shows per-request, per-token breakdown in Console. Free trial credits included."
Variant B — Anchor + scale incentive: "Start pay-as-you-go. Commitments available for predictable throughput and lower unit price (Dedicated contracts)."
Variant C — Developer-first simplicity: "Single per-token price for hosted inference; use autoscale and burst to avoid capacity surprises."

Recommended short explainer for cost estimator UI: "Estimate cost: enter avg prompt length and expected messages/sec. We show per-hour and monthly projections so you can prototype without surprises."

Sample pricing lines to test in email/web copy:
- "See estimated cost before you call — token estimator in Quickstart."
- "Free credits included for new signups. Stay on pay-as-you-go until you need reserved capacity."
- "Switching to Dedicated reduces unit price by up to X% for steady workloads."

Competitive callouts (notes for positioning vs alternatives):
- Distinguish from low-cost self-hosting: emphasize "no infra ops" + predictable SLAs and rollout tooling.
- Distinguish from model-access-only APIs: emphasize runtime optimizations (latency, batching), observability, and caching out-of-the-box.
- Distinguish from large hosted monopolies: emphasize lighter onboarding, clear dev ergonomics, and transparent cost visibility.

Sample objections and quick rebuttals for sales/dev docs:
- "How will I control costs?" -> "Estimator, per-call breakdown, token caps and usage alerts, and sample workloads showing typical monthly spend for a POC."
- "Can I keep data private?" -> "Yes — Dedicated and Private deployment options with VPC and KMS support."
- "What if latency matters?" -> "Managed model/runtime pairing and smart routing keep tail latency predictable; Console shows per-route latency percentiles."

Experiment plan (practical, 2-week cycles):
- Test A/B on landing hero: Hook variant (3-minute vs cost-first) -> measure signup->first-call time and first-hour call volume.
- Quickstart flow tweak: add inline cost estimator -> measure conversion to second call and session length.
- Pricing copy test in onboarding emails: "free credits + estimator" vs "single token price" -> measure activation and churn over first 7 days.

Metrics to track per experiment:
- api_key_created_rate, first_call_latency, calls_per_new_key_24h, cost_estimator_used (event), churn_7d, upgrade_interest_signal (in-bound contact or reserved capacity trial).

Content snippets for channel use (short):
- Email subject lines: "Spin up an LLM demo in 3 minutes (and see the cost before you call)", "Try inference — free credits + instant estimator"
- Hero CTAs: "Try quick demo", "Estimate cost", "Start with credits"

Tone guidance for copy:
- Keep it practical and engineer-friendly — show exact commands and numbers.
- Avoid marketing hyperbole — engineers distrust vague claims.
- Be explicit about tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs model size.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we show sample dollar estimates in hero (risk: numbers drift vs reality) or show relative cost bands?
- What is the preferred default example model for quickstarts (small but representative)?
- How granular should the estimator be in the first rollout? (tokens only vs tokens + infer-time CPU/GPU estimate)

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Design: produce two hero variants and estimator mock (Design: Maya) — 1 week.
- Engineering: wire a simple estimator endpoint and sample curl template (Evan) — 2 weeks.
- GTM: prepare email test cohort and event tracking (Priya + Liam) — 2 weeks.

Notes to reviewers:
- Keep feedback focused on testability and clarity. We want copy that can be A/B'd and measured.
- If you have strong language ideas (one-liners, micro-copy), add them inline under "content suggestions" in this doc.

Content suggestions (working list):
- "Run a sample generation in 3 minutes. Know the cost before you click."
- "Prototype on Hosted API. When ready, move to Dedicated without code changes."
- micro-copy for estimator tooltip: "Estimated tokens = avg prompt + avg completion length."

End of doc.
